summary: Deduplicated the eligible release-cache payloads on node1. All paths, bytes, ownership, and modes were preserved; protected and mutable files remain independent. The operation is idempotent and persisted through reboot.
actions_performed: Used the installed RHEL 10 util-linux hardlink 2.40.2 utility; no packages or system versions were changed.
Linked r1/payload.dat and r2/payload.dat, reclaiming one 1,856-byte logical payload allocation.
Kept mode-0600 private.dat and mutable/active.dat on independent inodes.
Restarted node1 safely and verified system, SSH, data, inode relationships, and idempotence after recovery.

evidence.summary: The dry run identified exactly one pair; the real pass linked it. Both payload paths now share inode 290760 with link count 2.

evidence.requirement: Preserve every pathname, byte, owner, and mode
evidence.summary: Before, after, and post-restart metadata and SHA-256 checksums match for all five paths.
private.dat remains mode 0600 with link count 1 and does not share the payload inode.
mutable/active.dat retains its separate inode, mode 0644, original checksum, and successfully opens for writing before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Storage reclaimed and later pass makes no changes
evidence.summary: Unique allocated blocks decreased from 40 to 32 512-byte blocks; repeated dry runs report Linked: 0 and Saved: 0 B.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel preserved
evidence.summary: RHEL 10.0, kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0, and util-linux-core 2.40.2-10.el10 remain installed after restart.
